IMPLEMENTED: one debrief for both formats and one death path.

WHERE THE LATER UNITS (wounds, ledger, record) PLUG IN
- Per-survivor effects: missions.js SURVIVOR_STEPS (missions.js:293, currently [classXp, condition]). debrief() (missions.js:307) runs every step for each survivor, in list order. A step is a function of { state, c, hp, casts, won, fallen, level, fights } that returns log lines or nothing. hp is the fraction of max HP at the end (Gate: run.members[id].hp, which already includes the quarter-HP rest after the last encounter; Field: fighter.hp / maxHp). casts is the run's spell count.
- Party-level effects: in debrief() after the survivor loop (the bonds block, then the loot multiplier).
- Callers build the survivor list: Missions.finish (missions.js:333) from run.members, and sortie.js debriefSquad(r, won, fallen) (sortie.js:407) from the squad actors. Returns { lootMult, lootBy, lines }; callers write the lines (Gate: run.log; Field: town log).
- Picker text: sortie.js partyFacts(c) (sortie.js:1063) is the one helper the party card calls; other units add their text there.
- Memorial record: the record literal in roster.js fallAll step 2 (roster.js:115). I store the bond snapshot as record.bonds = up to 4 positive bonds, strongest first, as { id, name, v, word, runs } (Bonds.snapshot, bonds.js:227). The record unit can slice it to two or extend the object.

WHAT CHANGED
1. missions.js: Missions.debrief(state, { survivors, fallen, won, level, fights }). Class XP = Classes.returned (unchanged: 1.5 won, 0.75 lost) + Classes.fought(c, min(fights, FOUGHT_CAP)); FOUGHT_CAP is derived as the longest Gate run, which is 3. Stamina cost = 25 + 1.5 x level for both formats (exported as Missions.missionStamina). Condition.spend with the run's cast count, then Condition.outcome(won, lost = fallen). Bonds: 'mission', 'won' if won, 'survived' if anyone died, else 'survived' at 0.5 on a loss (the block that was in settle(), now also run for Gate parties). lootMult = Classes.partyLoot of the survivors, lootBy = name of the class that sets it. Missions.finish no longer has inline class/condition calls. Gate rewards still = mission.reward x lootMult.
2. Death path (roster.js): Roster.fallAll(state, list, { cause, at, log }) and Roster.fall(state, c, opts) = fallAll of one. Order: (1) Bonds.snapshot of each dying character, (2) fall (leave roster, lock uuid and face, memorial record with bonds), (3) Bonds.mourn per fallen with Condition.adjustMorale as the morale callback, (4) Crew.mourn once. Characters in one call are snapshotted and removed together, so two friends dying in the same fight are in each other's record and do not grieve each other (a one-by-one version produced "Bruk lost Emeline" lines for a character who was dying in the same event; the test fails on that mutation). Idempotent per character: a character already on the memorial gets no second grief. Grief lines: "<friend> lost <dead> (<tier word>): morale -N", at most 4 per death, N is the amount applied so it can be checked on the MOR bar. Log goes to opts.log, else to Roster.setLog's logger, which game.js sets to logLine (game.js:418); this is what lets Sacrifice.apply and Missions.finish, which have no logger, still write lines.
3. Routed through it: Missions.finish (Roster.fallAll), sortie.js release(r) (Roster.fallAll, so settle() and abandon() share it), and the altar. sacrifice.js is outside my lock and unchanged: its Roster.fall call now grieves, so sacrificeTo needed no code change beyond a comment. Game.grieve is deleted (function and export); settleMission's Crew.mourn is deleted; sortie's Crew.mourn/grieve calls are deleted. game.js release(id) (letting someone go, not a death) now calls Bonds.tidy, its first caller.
4. sortie.js: settle() order is Crew.completed (before the deaths, so Crew.mourn scales the credited run exactly as before), release, debriefSquad, then payout. Kill drops are summed per kind and multiplied by lootMult once (contract fee not multiplied); settle line and result panel append "(drops x1.35, Thief)". run.fights is counted in resolve(), saved by persist(), defaults to 0 on old saves. abandon(): touched = !untouched(run) (a fight happened or somebody is down); touched and not already settled => debriefSquad(run, false, ...) (lost mission), untouched => nothing. A call-off does not credit the team (Crew.completed) and pays nothing.
5. field.js saveActor stores fighter.stats.casts in the combat record; sortie.js fighterFor restores it, so a reload keeps the cast count (rebuilt fighters started at 0).
6. condition.js: header corrected (it already said combat.js reads the pools; now also says where spend/outcome are called from), Condition.adjustMorale(c, delta), Condition.readyIn(c, restMult, fed, housed) = { ticks, limit } where limit is 'injury', 'stamina', or the pool kind. readyIn is tested against actually running Condition.tick until rested (exact tick match for 3 rest settings x 2 classes).

result.summary:
Retreat order implemented. Before contact (no hostile has seen the squad, no fight opened) the button is the free 'Call it off' (unchanged abandon(): frees the party, refunds a trial fee). After contact it reads 'Order a retreat' and calls the exported Field.retreat (existing withdraw path, exit goal, portal at extraction). The contract then ends through verdict(), settle() and Missions.debrief as a loss unless its terms are met before the squad is out (a win in that case; escorts and an already-escalated hardcore run usually end that way). There is no new settlement path. While the squad is withdrawing, by this order or its own decision, the button is disabled and reads 'Retreating'. If a fight is open the note under it says 'Retreat ordered; takes effect when the current fight ends.' Sortie.abandon stays exported. It is also offered in the UI as 'Abandon the run' once a withdrawal has run past Field.STRAGGLE (900 in-game s). The false board text 'Leaving the page abandons a run in progress' is replaced by accurate text about persist/resume and the call-off rule.

field.js changes: openSkirmish counts counters.fights (initialised to 0; older saves read 0). New contacted(s) = fights>0 or any actor.spotted. The 'quiet' side job resets only counters.spotted, so it cannot reopen the window. New retreat(s) refuses only when s.withdrew is set (plus no run or a finished run). withdraw() takes an 'ordered' flag: it is recorded in s.withdrew.ordered, and an order does not print the temper 'has been saying so' voice line. FieldAPI exports contacted, retreat and STRAGGLE.

sortie.js changes: exitState() returns free / order / retreating / stuck / over. exitOrder() is the click handler. It reads the state at click time, so a stale button drawn before contact sends the retreat order and does not free the squad. It also persists the order. EXIT table plus #sortie-exit-note drive label, disabled state and note. exitState and exitOrder are exported on window.Sortie.

result.openIssues:
1. The line-ending style differs by file and was preserved: sortie.js is CRLF, field.js and the new test are LF.

2. Deviations from the overseer's text, for you to accept or change. (a) Note wording: 'takes effect when the current fight ends' is shown only while a fight is open (full text: 'Retreat ordered; takes effect when the current fight ends.'). With no fight open that sentence would be false, so the note reads 'The squad is heading for the way home.' A squad that withdrew on its own with a fight open gets 'The squad has withdrawn on its own; it leaves when the current fight ends.' (b) The order is a loss only if the terms are not met. If they already are (the squad is pushing for stretch goals or walking home), the order banks the win through the normal verdict ('the terms were met, barely'). Escort (all-extract terms) and a hardcore run already escalated also end as wins. The note says 'loss unless its terms are met first'. (c) retreat() also refuses when there is no run or the run already has its result, as callBack does. (d) 'Contact' follows the approved proposal (a hostile has seen the squad OR a fight opened), so a sighting closes the free window and a trial fee can no longer be refunded after it. sortie.js untouched() still gates the refund inside abandon() for console use, and the button is 'free' only when both agree.
